interpretation: Statuses describe local source investigation, not deployed fixes.

issues.finding: Fresh save/replay bootstrap has 63 profiles but the reported session generated profile 65. New manual saves, autosaves and restart checkpoints retain the exact mission catalog. Cold loading checks the installed prefix and restores only exact generated profile definitions, transactionally. The disk-save regression covers three generated profiles and malformed catalog rejection. Older payloads lack this catalog. The archer report full log records the prior sequence DerbyExplorer (proto Derby), MultiTeamFourGrades, MultiTeamTwentyRobins, providing the exact generated-profile allocation order. New replay headers now retain the exact catalog in schema 65, with the same transactional validation as saves. A three-generated-mission regression covers JSONL and compact round trips and rejects conflicting installed or generated profiles without partial mutation. Schema 64 JSONL has an explicit upgrade path that preserves inputs without inventing the missing catalog; the supplied archer replay has now been reconstructed with its logged allocation order and a full-GOG base catalog. The upgrade worker replayed and verified all 28 recorded frames, preserving every input frame. Its new state hashes differ from the old report, including frame zero, so this is verified playback on the current engine/content, not proof of exact reporter-state reproduction. The recovery artifact remains local under tmp/report-investigation-oct7/f3aee4645e7d/catalog-recovered-verified.rhrec.jsonl; no affected profile-error save was attached. The client and ranking/verifier schema constants advance together to 65 and require a coordinated release. Campaign Manager also rejected missing profiles before cold-load admission; it now restores the saved catalog before constructing its view and presents an acknowledgement on incompatible saves instead of ending the game. Same-mission load routing now reconstructs immutable assets when the saved catalog extends the running one, and rejects a conflicting catalog.
Browser reports identify the old engine build. Existing resize filtering is present; engine commit alone does not identify the frontend shell revision.

Network adoption was rebuilding a serialized sequence index. Index repair now runs only for save loading. A regression verifies native snapshot byte identity and state hash with an index awaiting repair. No affected-session snapshot was attached, so the precise reporter case remains unverified.
These saves use version 75 while the current reader requires 97. No lossless migration implemented.

Report shows client H01_Lin_VL frame 688 with a corrected history rejecting a speech completion at replay frame 649. Failed dense or sparse reconstruction now returns an error instead of panicking; the client retains its live engine, pauses and requests an authoritative host snapshot. FIFO validation is unchanged; divergence is not silently accepted. Host reconstruction failure returns a session error.

The cache suppressed a sprite-bank read failure and continued with signature zero. Preserve the full error chain and fail mission preparation. The underlying reporter-specific file-open failure cannot be identified from the previous truncated error.

Reproduced by launching MultiTeamTwentyRobins with scripting disabled. Enemy-controlled heroes inherited character VIP flags, and the boss-only target restriction prevented selection of soldier targets. Restrict that rule to VIP soldiers; retain target boss protection.

additional_user_reports.finding: Only tactically controllable NPCs advanced glow timers; hostile soldiers retained alpha zero. Advance all NPC glows.

additional_user_reports.issue: Full NPC sprite shown inside buildings
additional_user_reports.finding: Render active indoor NPCs as outlines, with constant opacity when not carried.

additional_user_reports.issue: Single-character mission startup and starting scrolls missing for clients
additional_user_reports.finding: A joining client had no clock until receiving a periodic host state hash. The host can publish its initial hash before the peer connects, then wait at an early scroll before reaching the next hash boundary. BeginSim now supplies the initial clock anchor; snapshot admission clears stale clock state. A default two-peer regression verifies progress without any periodic hash, including a non-boundary start frame. An ignored full-GOG-data test runs H01_Lin_VL and S01_Not_VL with only Robin and verifies that both peers receive and acknowledge their startup scrolls (frames 1 and 17). The fixture substitutes socket delivery and rendering and advances engine frames directly; it does not establish graphical end-to-end behavior. The new S02_Lei_MP diagnostic with a working frame-zero popup used four heroes. The reported freeze build remains unknown, so the actual reporter case still needs a multiplayer retest.

additional_user_reports.issue: Non-host gesture combat only recognizes spin
additional_user_reports.finding: Drag capture omitted the press position. Two move events yielded only two samples and rejected a short D/E attack. Capture now seeds the press position; a down/move/move/up regression recognizes ThrustD. A real non-host session still needs confirmation.

additional_user_reports.issue: Tying an already tied enemy unties it
additional_user_reports.finding: The enable_unbinding rule intentionally lets the Tie ability untie bound NPCs.
Gameplay options show the localized difficulty. In-mission options use the running simulation difficulty, including on non-host clients.

No blanket four/five-character minimum exists. Lobby validation checks named required heroes and contextual abilities from the mission profile. Some missions need more heroes to satisfy those requirements; removing the checks without validating their scripts could create unwinnable missions.

User reports leaderboard deployment complete. The engine explicitly rejects coop.players > 1 in ranked policies, including AnyConfig; redeployment cannot remove that restriction. Mission-end presentation now browses the same mission and edition general board without a submission artifact and explains that co-op submissions are unsupported. Ranked admission remains unchanged; verified co-op submissions remain unimplemented.

Screenshot shows frame 12641 starts at timeline 12434 after previous frame ended at 12381. Mission-end browsing no longer requires client upload evidence. Recovery also left the open graphical frame at its old timeline; production regressions now verify forward/backward rebinding, correct input ownership, and reopened history capture. Replay schema 66 records actual snapshot adoption and successful late-input reconstruction as complete no-tick state-replacement records with exact native engine bytes and mandatory hashes. Playback adopts network state without saved-game fixups. Forward/backward JSONL and compact playback preserve correction hashes; production second-drain snapshot and dense/sparse rollback tests verify the emitted records. Ranked admission still rejects embedded recovery state. Older gap recordings contain no replacement state, so this does not reconstruct their missing history. Schema 64/65 JSONL upgrade preserves saved-game semantics. Client, API and verifier require a coordinated schema-66 release; none was deployed here.
